chunks: Saif al-Tammār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
One of our companions said to him: “We used to make up the daytime salat when we would stop between al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah.”

He said: “No. Allah knows His servants best when He granted the concession. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has only prescribed upon the traveler two rakʿahs; there is nothing before them nor after them, except salat al-layl upon your mount, wherever it takes you.”

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler subject to shortened prayer rulings
key_terms.رَخَّصَ: granted a concession or legal dispensation
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer prescribed for the traveler
key_terms.صَلَاةَ النَّهَارِ: the daytime prayer or prayers being made up
key_terms.صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer permitted even while mounted

ai.seo_question: What prayers may a traveler perform in addition to the shortened obligatory salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat during travel. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rejects making up daytime prayers between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ in this context and states that Allah has prescribed two rakʿahs for the traveler, with no prayer before or after them except the night prayer on one's mount.
